verifications.claim: University of Southern California (USC) is a private research university in Los Angeles.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The University of Southern California is a private research institution in Los Angeles." (R1); "The University of Southern California (USC)... is a premier private research university located in Los Angeles" (R2); "University of Southern California is a private institution..." (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly confirm USC as a private research university in Los Angeles.

verifications.claim: U.S. News & World Report ranks USC #28 in the 2026 National Universities ranking.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "In the 2026 edition of Best Colleges, University of Southern California is ranked No. #28 in National Universities." (R4); "USC is ranked 28th in the most recent U.S. News and World Report’s list of National Universities." (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match from US News source in R4 for 2026 ranking.

verifications.claim: The 2025-2026 application cycle for USC saw over 83,500 applications.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "In the 2024–25 admissions cycle, USC received approximately 83,500 applications" (R5); "11.2% of the 83,488 freshman applicants" (R10); "Around 83,500 prospective students applied" (R14)
verifications.reasoning: References confirm ~83,500 applications for the relevant recent cycle (Class of 2029, aligning with 2025 entry).

verifications.claim: USC's admission rate for the 2025-2026 application cycle is around 10.4%–11.2%.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "overall acceptance rate of about 11.2 percent" (R5); "11.2% of the 83,488" (R10); "acceptance rate... rose to 10.4%" (R14)
verifications.reasoning: References directly support the range for the Class of 2029 cycle.

verifications.claim: The middle 50% of admitted students at USC have an unweighted GPA between 3.79 and 4.00.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: References mention average GPAs (e.g., 3.80, 3.86) but no middle 50% unweighted GPA range.
